implementation_strategy: Paired sequential execution on 50 deterministic synthetic confirmatory tasks. For each task: (1) baseline pipeline = one hosted-model call to produce vendor-specific CLI config (direct_configuration_generation_v1) followed by deterministic verifier pass/fail; (2) guarded pipeline = initial hosted-model call to generate config; run CPU deterministic verifier; if verifier FAIL then issue a single repair model call with verifier assertions in prompt (total ≤2 model calls per task). All verification, pass/fail labeling, and scoring performed autonomously by the CPU-executable deterministic verifier. Immutable logging (prompts, model responses, verifier logs, timestamps, seeds) and SHA-256 hashing for all artifacts.
public_resources: Synthetic Intent→Configuration Task Suite (generated with fixed RNG seed; repository artifact)
CPU-executable deterministic verifier and reachability simulator (repository artifact)
Execution-logging and hash archive (to be published alongside paper)
task_manifest_strategy: Generate 50 confirmatory tasks deterministically: 10 synthetic topologies (seeded) × 5 tasks each; distribute vendor-CLI families equally across Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, Arista EOS. Record and hash the topology generator code, RNG seed stream, and final task files prior to execution.
transformation_manifest_strategy: Baseline: use canonical direct_configuration_generation_v1 prompt template to request vendor-specific CLI. Guarded: use generate_validate_repair_v1 template where verifier failure assertions are appended to prompt for a single repair attempt. Apply deterministic vendor templating and syntax-normalization prior to verifier ingestion. Verifier executed on CPU for every generated config; its assertions are machine-readable and inserted verbatim into repair prompts.
execution_batches: batch-1: tasks 1-50 (for each task run baseline then guarded consecutively to preserve pairing and deterministic logs)
randomisation_plan: No runtime random permutation. Task order fixed by the deterministic seed stream. Pairing preserved by executing baseline then guarded for each task sequentially.
caching_plan: Cache all model responses, verifier outputs, and normalized configs locally (immutable files with SHA-256 hashes) to avoid repeated provider calls and to ensure reproducibility.
failure_recovery_plan: Per-model-call: no automatic retries (maximum_attempts_per_call=1). On any model-call or verifier runtime failure mark the attempt as a technical failure, record error type and hash, and deterministically resample a replacement task from the pre-specified generator to preserve confirmatory N=50. All failures logged with deterministic replacement policy; no human intervention.
result_schema: Per-task paired episode record (JSON): {task_id, topology_id, vendor, intent, baseline_output, guarded_output_pre_repair, guarded_verifier_assertions_pre_repair, guarded_repair_output (if any), verifier_assertions_post_repair, final_verifier_pass: {baseline: bool, guarded: bool}, model_call_count: {baseline: int, guarded: int}, wall_time_seconds, artifact_hashes: {prompts, outputs, verifier_logs}, flags: [residual_uncertainty, contamination], technical_failure_flag}.
estimated_compute_notes: Model-call accounting: 50 tasks × 2 model calls/task (worst-case: initial + one repair in guarded pipeline) = 100 model calls total (estimated_model_calls and maximum_model_calls = 100). All verifier and simulator work is CPU-executable within the environment. Per-task wall-time timeout = 5 minutes; per-model-call timeout = provider default or 120s, whichever smaller. Total worst-case wall-clock for paired run expected < 1 day under hosted API latency; stays within capability_manifest maximum_wall_clock_days=7.
